headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared filesystem and broad egress; no documented hard isolation between Flowise and Khoj.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while Khoj reads indexed documents and personal notes. If Flowise outputs attacker-controlled content into shared files or retrieved notes, Khoj may ingest it as trusted context. The pair has a plausible shared-file bridge, so interaction risk exists beyond manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Flowise writes content into a directory that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj treats retrieved note text as instruction-bearing context
mitigations: Store Flowise outputs outside Khoj-indexed folders
Disable automatic indexing of Flowise-generated files
Add a manual review step before importing shared notes
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and also calls APIs. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive notes can flow from Khoj into Flowise prompts or tool calls, then out over Flowise's egress. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or uploaded files
IF Flowise flows send retrieved note contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep personal notes in a separate non-shared directory
Restrict Flowise flows from reading Khoj-managed files
Turn off external HTTP tools for flows handling sensitive data
Use distinct credentials and API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the filesystem and uses server datastore shared across instances; Khoj reads files and maintains a shared index across clients. Even without git or shell, both can mutate overlapping state if pointed at the same workspace or index, creating overwrite and stale-state conflicts. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF Flowise and Khoj are configured to use the same filesystem tree
IF Khoj indexes files that Flowise also rewrites
mitigations: Separate writable directories for each agent
Make Flowise outputs append-only
Pause Khoj reindexing during Flowise writes
Use file-level locks where available
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that may consume those outputs as context. If Khoj treats Flowise-produced text as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream answers or actions. No verification or provenance controls are documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Khoj uses Flowise-generated text as retrieved evidence or system-like instructions
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require source links for any Flowise-generated claims
Add a verification prompt before Khoj acts on Flowise output
Limit Flowise to drafting, not final decisions
Review high-impact outputs manually
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. If personal or regulated data is routed from Khoj into Flowise flows, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches because neither profile documents aligned compliance controls or deletion handling. The risk is compliance drift rather than a proven residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated notes or personal data are indexed by Khoj
IF Flowise stores or logs those contents in chatflow outputs or provider calls
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through shared flows
Minimize logging on both systems
Document retention settings for each agent
Separate datasets by sensitivity class
requires-engineering: align deletion and retention workflows
